All 9 tests pass (5 in test_t1, 4 in test_t2). Changes are confined to `reports/render.py`. **What changed** - **Added `"csv"` format.** Header row, then one comma-joined line per row, no title. - **Added `"html"` format.** `

title

`, ``, a `
` header row, one `` row per data row, `
`, each on its own line. - **Added `render_many(reports, fmt)`.** Returns `render(r, fmt)` for each report, in order. It's exported in `__all__`. - **Changed the trailing-newline behaviour of `render`.** This was forced by the new test. `test_render_many` expects `"B\n\n1"` with no trailing newline, but the old implementation terminated every line with `"\n"`. At the same time, the existing `test_empty_rows` still needs the blank line after the title to survive `splitlines()` when there are no rows. The formulation satisfying both is "title line, blank line, then rows joined by newlines". So renderers now return the full string rather than a list of lines, and the shared `_with_header` helper builds `title + "\n\n" + "\n".join(body)`. One consequence worth knowing: a titled report with zero rows renders as `"T\n\n"`, while a report with rows has no trailing newline. The docstring on `render` states this. The registry-based composition design (Approach B) is unchanged. Nothing under `tests/` was touched, and nothing has been committed.
